# Engagement

ROAR-Word is a timed lexical decision task: the child sees a letter string
and decides as fast as they can whether it is a real word. Children who
tap through without reading answer near chance, or very fast. Runs with
accuracy below 40% or a median response time under 500 ms are dropped
before any analysis on this site (`clean_levante_latest()` in `common.R`).

```{r swr-engagement}
swr_runs_all <- load_levante_latest_trials("swr") |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_rt = median(rt_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(scores_all |> filter(task_id == "swr") |>
               distinct(run_id, dataset, language, score), by = "run_id") |>
  mutate(dropped = accuracy < 0.4 | median_rt < 500)
swr_drop <- swr_runs_all |>
  filter(!is.na(score)) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(n = n(), dropped = mean(dropped), .groups = "drop")
swr_unscored <- scores_all |>
  filter(task_id == "swr") |>
  distinct(run_id, language, score) |>
  group_by(lang = substr(language, 1, 2)) |>
  summarise(n = n(), unscored = sum(is.na(score)), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r swr-engagement-plot, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-swr-engagement
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy against median response time for every scored ROAR-Word run; runs outside the dashed lines are dropped as non-engaged."
swr_runs_all |>
  filter(!is.na(score), median_rt < 5000) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median_rt, y = accuracy, colour = dropped)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, lty = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 500, lty = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#CC3311", `FALSE` = "grey45"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Median response time (ms)", y = "Accuracy")
```

Share of scored runs dropped:
`r with(by_ds(swr_drop), paste0(dataset_labels_named[dataset], " ", fmt_pct(dropped), " (of ", fmt_n(n), ")", collapse = "; "))`.

# Open issues

`r k <- sum(item_lang$below_chance); if (k > 0) paste0("- ", k, " item-language combinations are answered below chance (@fig-item-health). In lexical decision this need not mean a wrong key: children can reject rare real words and accept pseudowords that look like real words. These items are worth reviewing, but they may be working as intended.") else ""`
`r de <- filter(swr_unscored, lang == "de"); if (nrow(de) == 1 && de$unscored == de$n) paste0("- None of the ", fmt_n(de$n), " German runs has a score in this release, although a German item bank is calibrated (", sum(items$lang == "de"), " items).") else ""`
- `r fmt_pct(mean(item_key(trials) %in% item_key(thin_items)), 0)` of
  responses go to items calibrated on fewer than `r min_calib` responses.
  With a large bank of words seen rarely, many item parameters rest on
  little data.
- The engagement rule and its effect on scores are studied in
  [ROAR-Word engagement](../studies/2026-07_roar-word-engagement/roar_word.qmd).
